summary.en: Distinguish category prediction from numeric prediction and compare probabilities, labels and a held-out classifier score.
summary.bn: কোন দলে পড়বে তা predict করো; লেবেল, probability ও নতুন ডেটায় classifier-এর score আলাদা করে বোঝো।

examples.title: Apply an explicit two-group rule before using a library
examples.explanationHtml: This explicit teaching rule places a vertical fence at size score three. It agrees with all six displayed labels. Its perfect training result describes those rows; it is not a measurement on unseen fruit.

examples.title: Fit, predict and score with a one-question classifier
examples.explanationHtml: The fitted tree gives the same query label and training score. On these symmetric points it may select an equally effective cut on the other feature. A learned boundary need not be uniquely determined by a tiny dataset.

examples.title: Reserve unseen iris flowers before measuring accuracy
examples.explanationHtml: Iris has three categories. A stratified split keeps every category in both subsets. Test flowers are not passed to fit, so the score measures a different question from training accuracy.

practice.title: Turn a probability into a stated binary label
practice.statementHtml: Read probability p and threshold t, both finite and between zero and one. Predict one when p ≥ t, otherwise zero. Print invalid for malformed or out-of-range values. The equality rule is part of the contract.

practice.title: Measure a small prediction list
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 1 through 20, then n true/predicted label pairs, each label 0 or 1. Print correct COUNT and accuracy to three decimals. Reject missing or malformed input with invalid.

practice.title: Choose prediction types
practice.statementHtml: Classify predicting a fruit name, a rent amount and one of three iris species.
hints: Look at what the target means.
practice.answerHtml: Fruit name is classification; it is binary only with exactly two allowed names. Rent amount is regression. Three iris species form multiclass classification. The target meaning, not the number of features, decides the task.

practice.title: Interpret a confident error
practice.statementHtml: A model assigns mango probability 0.9 but the fruit is an apple. Why is this possible?
hints: A model estimate can be wrong.
practice.answerHtml: The model estimates uncertainty from learned patterns and assumptions. It can be confidently wrong on unusual or shifted data. Check calibration and representative held-out performance rather than treating one large score as a guarantee.

quiz.prompt: Read the plot: which category lies entirely left of the size-three fence?
quiz.explanation: Apple points have size one or two; mango points have size four or five.

quiz.prompt: Read row B: which label follows the largest probability?
quiz.explanation: For B, apple probability 0.6 exceeds mango probability 0.4. Selecting one label hides that uncertainty.

keyPoints.en: Classification predicts a category rather than a continuous amount.
keyPoints.bn: ক্লাসিফিকেশন ধারাবাহিক পরিমাণের বদলে একটি category predict করে।

keyPoints.en: Binary and multiclass describe the number of target categories.
keyPoints.bn: Binary ও multiclass দিয়ে target category-এর সংখ্যা বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: A probability retains uncertainty that a hard label hides.
keyPoints.bn: Probability-তে uncertainty দেখা যায়; শুধু লেবেলে সেই তথ্য থাকে না।

keyPoints.en: A decision boundary separates different predicted labels.
keyPoints.bn: Decision boundary-এর দুই অঞ্চলে মডেলের লেবেল আলাদা হয়।
আলাদা রাখা নতুন উদাহরণে মডেলের ফল মাপো।

examQuestions.question: Distinguish binary classification, multiclass classification and regression.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Binary classification predicts one of two categories. Multiclass predicts one of more than two. Regression predicts an amount such as rent. A target encoded as 0/1 remains categorical when the numbers name groups.

examQuestions.question: Compute accuracy for eight predictions with six correct labels.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Accuracy is 6/8 = 0.75, or 75%. State which rows supplied the score. A training score is not an independent measurement of future performance.

examQuestions.question: Explain a probability and its thresholded label.
examQuestions.answerHtml: A probability expresses an estimated chance. A threshold converts it into a hard decision. At an inclusive 0.5 threshold, 0.8 becomes one and 0.4 becomes zero. Moving the threshold changes decisions without refitting scores; estimated chances are not guarantees.
